one_line: Titular Gond princes of Garha-Mandla, martyred in the 1857 uprising at Jabalpur.

appearance.age_look: Shankar appears around his late 60s, lean but upright with a dignified bearing; Raghunath appears in his early 30s, athletic and slightly taller, standing protectively near his father.
appearance.face: Shankar has a narrow oval face with deep-set eyes, a lined medium-brown complexion, a neatly trimmed grey moustache and short greying beard, and a calm, resolute default expression; Raghunath has a slightly broader oval face, warm medium-brown complexion, sharp dark eyes, a straight nose, a thinner black moustache and light stubble, with a determined yet respectful default expression.
appearance.hair: Both wear their hair pulled back and tied in low knots under simple white cotton pagris; Shankar’s hair is mostly grey beneath his turban, while Raghunath’s is black, with the turban tails falling neatly over the left shoulder.
appearance.costume: Shankar wears a long off-white cotton angarkha reaching mid-calf, tied at the side with visible cloth ties, over a pale saffron cotton uttariya shawl draped from the left shoulder across the torso; he has loose white churidar trousers and plain brown leather sandals, with minimal jewellery limited to a simple brass ring and a slender beaded tulsi mala at his neck; Raghunath wears a slightly shorter knee-length light-cream cotton angarkha, a muted indigo cotton waistcoat over it with simple wooden toggles, narrow white churidar trousers, and dark brown leather mojari-style shoes, plus a plain dark-red cotton sash (patka) wrapped at his waist, and a single thin metal bangle on his right wrist, both men’s garments slightly worn but clean, reflecting their status as pensioned nobles rather than reigning kings.
appearance.signature: A single, slightly weathered but carefully kept talwar with a steel blade, traditional Indo-Muslim hilt with a disc pommel and knuckle guard, and a plain brown leather scabbard, usually carried in Raghunath’s left hand while Shankar rests one hand on the hilt.

ref_desc: Shankar Shah is an older, lean man in an off-white angarkha, saffron shawl, white churidar and white turban beside his son Raghunath Shah, a younger athletic man in a cream angarkha, indigo waistcoat, dark-red sash, white turban and brown shoes, together holding a single brown-sheathed talwar.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Shankar Shah and Raghunath Shah standing together as Gond-descended princes in 1857 Jabalpur: Shankar is an older, lean man with a narrow lined face, medium-brown complexion, deep-set eyes, grey moustache and short beard, wearing his greying hair tied under a simple white cotton turban; he is dressed in a long off-white cotton angarkha reaching mid-calf, tied at the side, a pale saffron cotton shawl draped from his left shoulder across his torso, loose white churidar trousers and plain brown leather sandals, with only a thin tulsi bead necklace and a simple brass ring for jewellery, his expression calm and resolute. Raghunath is taller and athletic with a slightly broader oval face, medium-brown complexion, sharp dark eyes, a straight nose, and a thin black moustache with light stubble; his black hair is tied under a matching white turban with tails falling over his left shoulder. He wears a knee-length light-cream cotton angarkha, a muted indigo cotton waistcoat fastened with simple toggles, narrow white churidar trousers, and dark brown leather mojari-style shoes, with a plain dark-red cotton sash (patka) wrapped at his waist and a single thin metal bangle on his right wrist, his expression determined yet respectful as he stands close to his father. Give them a shared signature weapon: one slightly weathered but carefully kept talwar with a steel blade, traditional hilt and plain brown leather scabbard, held in Raghunath’s left hand while Shankar lightly rests his right hand on the hilt, emphasizing their unity; use a muted palette of off-white, saffron, indigo, dark red and brown leather, and present them front-facing with consistent anime-style proportions so the same costumes, face shapes, turbans and weapon can be redrawn identically in many panels.
